messages:
incident-bot: Paging: P1 — SLO breach detected: streaming p99 latency > 3s for the past 6m on prod-us-west. Auto-alert triggered by latency-slo-watchers. @taylor you are oncall. :rotating_light:

taylor: I’m on it. grabbing current dashboards and hit list. What’s the scope?

maria: seeing a surge in p99 and a bunch of `streaming stall` traces from the runtime. Affected routes: /v1/stream and /v1/chat/stream, mostly long-context requests. p95 also creeping up.

ken: quick note — I’m seeing KV cache misses spike at the same time for a subset of requests. Could be correlated with node-level dropouts.

alex: telemetry shows a single GPU host (gpu-node-az3-112) with intermittent device reset events in the last 10m. NVML shows increasing correctable ECC counts prior to resets. Posting relevant snippet.

alex: ```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] nvml: ecc_corrected_count: 42
[2026-03-15T14:03:04Z] nvml: ecc_corrected_count: 117
[2026-03-15T14:04:50Z] driver: device_reset: minor
[2026-03-15T14:05:01Z] runtime: streaming-stall detected, rpc latency 3.6s
```

maria: customers impacted? sara?

sara: Support triage — ~8 customer sessions reported slow responses over last 7m, 2 on paid enterprise accounts (acct-A12, acct-B07). All report streaming stalls rather than outright 5xx failures. Logging shows retries from SDK clients.

taylor: Ok. Mitigation plan: 1) isolate gpu-node-az3-112, 2) re-route new streaming sessions off that node, 3) enable fallback model pool (cpu-fallback) for in-flight long contexts if needed, 4) reduce batching on the streaming tier to reduce tail. Can we do node isolate quickly?

infra-bot: Command suggestion: `infractl node evacuate gpu-node-az3-112 --grace-period=30s --drain-requests`

ken: I’ll run evacuate. Doing a fast drain with `--force-routing` so router will stop assigning new streams. Executing now.

ken: (runs) ```
$ infractl node evacuate gpu-node-az3-112 --grace-period=30s --force-routing
Evacuation started. Active streams will be migrated where possible. Router policy updated to exclude gpu-node-az3-112.
```

maria: Router update observed: node excluded from pool. Diff in route table: removed 10/10 backends for az3-112. New requests are routing around it.

alex: We still have in-flight sessions pinned to that node — migration is in progress but a few long contexts are still streaming. Those sessions show stalls during device_reset windows.

taylor: Next: reduce batch size / max_concurrent_tokens for streaming service to cut per-token latency. Change below will be applied to streaming config.

ken: Pushing config tweak now. ```
PATCH /api/v1/configs/streaming
{ "batching.max_batch_size": "16", "batching.max_tokens_per_batch": "512" }
```

infra-bot: Config change applied. New pool instances will pick up settings within 45s.

maria: Telemetry: after node exclude + batch size change, p95 dropped from 850ms -> 420ms, p99 down from 3.4s -> 1.7s in the last 2m. Good sign.

alex: GPU node logs still show ECC corrected spikes earlier, followed by a driver minor reset. NVML now stable since exclusion. Suspect flaky DIMM or thermal coupling.

ken: I recommend we mark the node as quarantined and schedule a hardware ticket. `infractl node annotate gpu-node-az3-112 quarantine:hw-failure`

ken: (runs) ```
$ infractl node annotate gpu-node-az3-112 quarantine:hw-failure
Node gpu-node-az3-112 marked quarantine:hw-failure
```

infra-bot: Node marked. Auto-scaling for the dedicated pool triggered +2 replacement GPUs. New nodes healthy.

sara: Notifying affected customers with temporary mitigation note — telling them we’re routing around problematic hardware and will follow up.

maria: Ops note: We should also keep an eye on ECC correction rates across the cluster; sending a short query to surface any other nodes with rising counts.```\n$ promql: sum by(node)(increase(nvml_ecc_corrected_total[5m])) > 20
```

alex: Running that — only gpu-node-az3-112 crossed the threshold. No siblings flagged.

taylor: Good. For now the immediate mitigation worked. Remaining actions: 1) hardware ticket (infra), 2) post-incident customer follow-up (support), 3) run longer kv-cache warmup to avoid cold-miss correlated stalls (runtime), 4) add alert rule to detect ECC surge earlier. Assigning owners: infra -> ken, support -> sara, runtime -> maria.

ken: I’ve opened HW ticket #HW-9872 for replacement and firmware check. ETA next business day for physical swap; will request expedited if further regressions.

sara: Customer notices sent for acct-A12 and acct-B07. Template saved to drafts. Will send after final wording approved by taylor.

maria: I’ll add a regression alert: `nvml_ecc_corrected_total` P90 delta alert + a routing fallback runbook. Also will schedule a small experiment to warm KV cache earlier for long-context endpoints.

taylor: Handing to next oncall in 30m. Summary for handoff: cause = flaky GPU (ECC correctables + driver reset) causing intermittent streaming stalls -> SLO breach. Mitigations applied: excluded node, reduced batch size, enabled cpu-fallback routing, opened HW ticket, customers notified. Monitoring p99 closely.

taylor: @ken @maria @sara anything to add for handoff?

ken: Nothing else. I’ll follow hardware and update ticket with replacement node id.

maria: I’ll keep watch on p99 for 2h and post updates to #incidents. I’ll also add the new alert rule.

sara: I’ll send customer follow-ups and include mitigation details + ETA for full remediation.

incident-bot: Incident state update: mitigated -> degraded. p99 returned under threshold. Continue monitoring.

taylor: Ok handing off at 2026-03-15T14:20Z to next oncall. Marking thread for postmortem grouping. :white_check_mark:
